name: WISE BPIC'19 norm draft v1.1
description: Flow-aware purchase-to-pay norm for the BPI Challenge 2019 log: 29 constraints in seven layers, four role-based views (Finance, Logistics, Compliance, Automation). Scoring mode layer_balanced; lag constraints measure from the first activation to the first response in the case and are not applicable when an endpoint is missing; order constraints are precedence checks. Draft v1.1 (cycle 2, R1-10): the merged invoice-before-goods expectation of v1.0 is split into a commercial expectation on the vendor's invoice date and a compliance expectation on the invoice posting; a cleared-before-goods expectation is added for both three-way flows; the payment-term activity uses the log's spelling. The weights of the three new expectations are placeholders until an owner calibrates them; every other expectation and threshold is unchanged from v1.0.

changes.rationale: The v1.0 expectation merges the vendor's invoice date ('Vendor creates invoice') with the invoice posting ('Record Invoice Receipt'). On BPIC 2019 it is missed by 51.7 % of DF1 items with both evidences, almost entirely through the vendor's date: by the vendor's invoice date 53.6 % of DF1 items with both dates are early (37.9 % of all DF1 items), by the posting date 0.0 % (measured 2026-09-06 with log primitives, first evidence against first goods or service receipt). The challenge reports measured the posting (5.0 % in DF1 under the HPI rule 6). One expectation cannot say which of the two it means.

The vendor's invoice date should not precede the first goods or service receipt in GR-based flows; a pattern of the vendor's invoicing practice (invoice at dispatch, transport time), not a posting error. Expected on BPIC 2019: about 54 % of DF1 items with both dates (10,722 items), 37.9 % of all 15,182 DF1 items.
changes.weight: 0.7, placeholder: half the v1.0 weight, because the commercial half is not an audit finding; to be set by the process owner

changes.rationale: The invoice posting should not precede the first goods or service receipt in GR-based flows (GR-based invoice verification). Expected on BPIC 2019: 0.0 % of the 11,128 DF1 items with both postings; the HPI report's 5.0 % counts its own rule.
changes.weight: 1.4, placeholder: the v1.0 weight, because this is the three-way-match compliance point; to be confirmed by the process owner

changes.rationale: The challenge reports' 'invoice cleared before goods receipt' rule (HPI rule 4: 4.58 % of DF1 cases), which v1.0 has no expectation for. By posting timestamps the share is 0.0 % of 9,675 DF1 items and 0.05 % of 173,133 DF2 items with both events (measured 2026-09-06), so the reports' figure is not reproduced by log timestamps; the expectation is kept as the audit rule it states and will report near zero on this log.
changes.weight: 1.2, placeholder; to be set by finance

changes.rationale: The CSV's spelling (7 events); with the v1.0 spelling Norm.check reports an activity that never occurs and the expectation is never violated.
'Vendor creates credit memo' does not occur in the BPIC 2019 CSV; the expectation is kept so that the norm stays complete for logs that carry it, and Norm.check reports it as never occurring.

Thresholds, weights, applicability and layer weights are the paper's. In layer_balanced scoring the split changes the within-layer shares of L2 (six expectations instead of four), so v1.1 backlogs differ from v1.0 even where nothing else changed.

notes: Norm draft for the norm builder (R1-10); the paper's norm stays byte-identical in p2p_bpic19.json.

L1_closure_completeness.expectation: Every ordered item is received, invoiced and paid, so that nothing stays open longer than it should.
L1_closure_completeness.meaning_when_missed: An item is missing one of its expected milestones: goods were ordered but no receipt is posted, goods were received but no invoice arrived, or an invoice was recorded but never cleared.
L1_closure_completeness.why_it_matters: Open items hide liabilities and unpaid vendors, distort accruals at period end and make the purchase order history unusable for planning; every open item is a call, an e-mail or a manual clean-up later.
L1_closure_completeness.how_detected: Three presence rules on the flows where the milestone is expected: invoice evidence on invoice-bearing items, a payment on invoice-bearing items, and a goods or service receipt on three-way items. Items still open at the end of the data are flagged separately as not yet judgeable.

usual_reasons.check: goods received without invoice evidence after 60 days, by vendor; invoice documents without item link in the source system

usual_reasons.check: service items with an invoice but no service entry sheet, by purchasing group

usual_reasons.text: The item was deleted, blocked or closed by reducing the quantity instead of receiving it
usual_reasons.check: deletion, block and quantity-change events on the open items

usual_reasons.text: The item category expects a milestone that this purchase never has (framework, consignment)
usual_reasons.check: ask the buyer whether the document type needs a receipt or an item-level clearing at all

L2_flow_discipline.missed_label: steps out of order for this flow type
L2_flow_discipline.missed_label_de: Schritte in falscher Reihenfolge für diesen Flusstyp
L2_flow_discipline.expectation: Requisition, order, receipt and invoice happen in the order the flow type prescribes: in GR-based flows the invoice follows the receipt, in invoice-first flows the payment block is released only after the goods arrive, two-way and consignment items show no postings they should not have.
L2_flow_discipline.meaning_when_missed: Goods or services were bought or paid outside the agreed channel, an invoice was processed before delivery was confirmed, a block was released before the goods arrived, or an item is typed as a flow it does not follow.
L2_flow_discipline.why_it_matters: Off-contract prices, no leverage over the vendor, payment for goods not received, audit findings on the three-way match, and repair work in accounts payable to fix documents after the fact.
L2_flow_discipline.how_detected: Order rules per flow type: invoice evidence not before the first receipt in GR-based flows; payment block released after the first receipt in invoice-first flows; no receipt postings on two-way items; no item-level clearing on consignment items.

L3_timeliness_ageing.missed_label_de: zu lange Wartezeit zwischen den Schritten
L3_timeliness_ageing.expectation: Receipts, invoices, block releases and payments follow each other within the agreed number of days.
L3_timeliness_ageing.meaning_when_missed: Items age between two steps; invoices wait for a receipt or a release, released invoices wait for a payment run, and vendors wait for their money.
L3_timeliness_ageing.why_it_matters: Lost early-payment discounts, vendor escalations and delivery stops, working capital tied up or paid out too early, and a backlog that accounts payable works through by hand.
L3_timeliness_ageing.how_detected: Time-between-steps rules with a target and a tolerance: receipt to invoice in GR-based flows (target 10 days, tolerance to 30 in the paper's norm), invoice to payment (30 days, tolerance to 90), receipt to block release and release to payment in invoice-first flows (2 and 5 days). Each item scores between met and fully missed according to how far beyond the target it is.

usual_reasons.check: ask accounts payable for the payment-run calendar and any period-end holds

L4_rework_instability.expectation: Each step is posted once and stays; no repeated receipts, invoices, approvals, confirmations or term changes on the same item.
L4_rework_instability.meaning_when_missed: The same step was posted several times or changed afterwards, so the item was handled more than once and its history is unstable.
L4_rework_instability.why_it_matters: Every repeat is a manual touch, a matching problem and a chance for a duplicate payment; unstable commitments make planning and vendor evaluation unreliable.
L4_rework_instability.how_detected: Count rules with a tolerated number and a saturation point: receipt events (more than two count), invoice receipts (more than one), approval changes (any), payment-term changes (any), vendor confirmations and confirmed-date changes in the baseline.

L5_exceptions_corrections.expectation: Cancellations of receipts and invoices, item deletions, blocks and vendor memos are the exception, not part of the normal path.
L5_exceptions_corrections.meaning_when_missed: A posting had to be undone or corrected with a separate document; the item did not go straight through.
L5_exceptions_corrections.why_it_matters: Corrections cost effort in the warehouse and in accounts payable, they delay payment, they carry audit risk, and memos signal disputes with the vendor.
L5_exceptions_corrections.how_detected: Rules that expect an activity never to occur: cancelled invoice receipt, cancelled goods receipt, deleted item, vendor debit memo, vendor credit memo, and in the baseline item blocks, manual payment blocks and interface failures.

L6_value_commercial.missed_label: price or quantity changed after ordering
L6_value_commercial.missed_label_de: Preis oder Menge nach Bestellung geändert
L6_value_commercial.expectation: The price and quantity on the order are the ones agreed with the vendor before ordering, and invoiced values match ordered and received values, especially on high-value items.
L6_value_commercial.meaning_when_missed: The order was edited after it went out, or correction documents moved the value of the item; what is paid may not be what was agreed.
L6_value_commercial.why_it_matters: Money paid above the agreed price, no audit trail of the negotiation, and invoice verification that passes because the order was changed to fit the invoice.
L6_value_commercial.how_detected: Count rules on price and quantity changes (any change counts, two saturate), value-weighted rules that count memos and price changes more on high-exposure items, and the spread of the cumulative net worth across the item's postings; these are commercial-risk indicators, not audit findings.

L7_effort_automation.expectation: Items pass from order to payment with as few manual touches, hand-offs and events as the flow needs.
L7_effort_automation.meaning_when_missed: People had to intervene several times on the item, several people touched it, or the item collected a long chain of events.
L7_effort_automation.why_it_matters: Effort in purchasing and accounts payable, waiting time at each hand-off, and errors introduced by manual work; the touchless rate is the lever for automation.
L7_effort_automation.how_detected: Threshold rules on derived counts: manual touches by named users (more than 4, saturating at 10), distinct human users (more than 2), total events (more than 10) and the manual share of events (above half); batch users are excluded by name.

c_l6_change_price.expectation: The price on the order is not changed after the item is created.

c_l6_high_exposure_memo.expectation: Correction documents (vendor debit or credit memos) do not occur on items with high value at stake.
c_l6_high_exposure_memo.meaning_when_missed: A memo landed on a high-value item; the same event that would be minor on a small item is financially material here.
c_l6_high_exposure_memo.why_it_matters: Memos on the largest items carry most of the money in disputes and corrections; value weighting puts them first.
c_l6_high_exposure_memo.how_detected: A threshold rule on a derived value that is the memo indicator times the item's exposure scaled to the 95th percentile; any positive value counts, full exposure saturates.

c_l6_networth_volatility.expectation: The cumulative net worth of the item stays stable across its postings.
